comment: Maturity models and compliance checklists that evaluate technical exchange capability alone create a structural blind spot. A health system can achieve high technical standards conformance (e.g., FHIR profile compliance) while front-line care coordination remains stagnant or decays. Without an operationalized metric for transaction resolution, national architectures cannot verify whether clinical value is being generated.

public.text: Maturity models and compliance checklists that evaluate technical exchange capability alone create a structural blind spot. A health system can achieve high technical standards conformance (e.g., FHIR profile compliance) while front-line care coordination remains stagnant or decays. Without an operationalized metric for transaction resolution, national architectures cannot verify whether clinical value is being generated.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to conformance and performance metrics guidance: “The performance evaluation framework for DPI-H should recommend Loop-Closure Rates as the primary success metric for national digital infrastructure. A transaction (such as a referral, prescription, or diagnostic order) is only considered successful when it closes securely at both endpoints of the clinical workflow, with transactional visibility provided to the patient.”
